Container.Name: Requestarr

Branch.TagDescription: Pre-release. The only published tag while no stable release exists.

Container.Overview: Requestarr is a shared request and availability portal for movies, TV, music, audiobooks and games. People sign in with your identity provider (OIDC), ask for something once, and everyone who wants it is notified when it appears in your Plex, Jellyfin, Navidrome, Audiobookshelf or RomM library. It does not download or acquire anything. Before installing you need three things it does not bundle: a PostgreSQL database, an identity provider that speaks OIDC over https, and a reverse proxy that serves Requestarr over https. Library and provider credentials are entered in the app after you sign in (Settings, Integrations), not here; if you prefer environment variables, use Unraid's "add another variable" option (Add another Path, Port, Variable, Label or Device) at the bottom of this form and set the matching REQUESTARR_ variable. No appdata folder is needed: everything is stored in PostgreSQL.
Container.Requires: A PostgreSQL database, an https OIDC identity provider and an https reverse proxy. None of them is included. To reach other containers by name (for example PostgreSQL), set Network Type to a user-defined Docker network; the default bridge cannot resolve container names.

Config.Name: Web Port
Config.Description: Required. Port on this server where the Requestarr web interface listens. Point your https reverse proxy at it. Change it only if 8080 is already used by another container.

Config.Name: Database Host
Config.Description: Required. Where your PostgreSQL server is: its container name (for example postgres) or the server's address. A container name only resolves when both containers are on the same user-defined Docker network (see Network Type); the default bridge cannot resolve names.

Config.Name: Database Port
Config.Description: Optional. The port PostgreSQL listens on. Leave at 5432 unless your database uses another port.

Config.Name: Database Name
Config.Description: Required. The name of the empty PostgreSQL database you created for Requestarr. Create the database and a user that owns it first.

Config.Name: Database User
Config.Description: Required. The PostgreSQL user that owns that database, for example requestarr.

Config.Name: Database Password
Config.Description: Required. The password of that PostgreSQL user. Requestarr escapes it itself, so any characters are fine. Keep it private.

Config.Name: Database SSL Mode
Config.Description: Optional. How the connection to PostgreSQL is encrypted: disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca or verify-full. Leave empty for the driver default. Use require or stronger if the traffic crosses a network you do not control.

Config.Name: Database URL (override)
Config.Description: Optional. A complete PostgreSQL connection URL. When set it replaces the database fields above, which are then ignored. Most installs leave it empty. It can contain the password, so it is masked.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Required. The https address people type to reach Requestarr, normally your reverse proxy, for example https://requests.example.com. Sign-in redirects back to this address, so it must match exactly. http is not accepted.

Config.Name: OIDC Issuer
Config.Description: Required. The https issuer URL of your OIDC identity provider, for example https://id.example.com/realms/requestarr for Keycloak. Requestarr finds the provider's settings from this address.

Config.Name: OIDC Client ID
Config.Description: Required. The client ID of the confidential client you created for Requestarr in your identity provider. Its redirect URI is your Public URL followed by /api/v1/auth/callback.

Config.Name: OIDC Client Secret
Config.Description: Required. The client secret of that OIDC client, copied from your identity provider. Keep it private.

Config.Name: Session Secret
Config.Description: Required. A random secret that signs login sessions, at least 32 bytes. Generate one in a terminal with: openssl rand -base64 48 . Changing it signs everyone out. Do not reuse the master key.

Config.Name: Master Key
Config.Description: Required. Encrypts the library and provider credentials that you save in Settings, Integrations; they apply as soon as you save them, with no container restart. Exactly 32 random bytes written as 64 hex characters or as base64. Generate one in a terminal with: openssl rand -base64 32 . Back it up separately from the database: without it saved credentials cannot be read and must be entered again. Changing it has the same effect.

Config.Name: Environment
Config.Description: Optional. Leave this at production. It turns on the safety rules for a real server: the public URL and the OIDC issuer must use https, and library addresses must use https unless they are on your private network. Only a developer's test setup uses anything else.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: Optional. How much the server logs: debug, info, warn or error. Leave at info unless you are troubleshooting.

Config.Name: Extra Private Networks
Config.Description: Optional. Comma-separated CIDRs and host name suffixes, for example 192.0.2.0/24,.mylab. Library addresses on these networks may use http:// in addition to the private ranges and names that are always allowed (LAN addresses, single-word container names, .local, .lan, .internal, .home.arpa). Anything else needs https. A library token sent over http is not encrypted on the network.
